chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abil Jarud, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

He said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, if the scholar of your Household passes away, by what sign is the one who comes after him recognized?' He said: 'By guidance and serenity, and the testimony of the Family of Muhammad to his excellence, and he is not asked about anything between his two temples except that he answers regarding it.'

key_terms.الِاطِّرَاقِ: Serenity or calmness (often interpreted as composure or tranquility)
key_terms.بَيْنَ صَدَفَيْهِ: Between his two temples (idiom for comprehensive knowledge or intellect)

ai.seo_question: What are the four signs to recognize the next Imam or scholar after the previous one?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* establishes the criteria for *al-Nass* (designation) or recognition of the Imam, emphasizing that divine guidance and a serene demeanor are internal markers, while the acknowledgment by the *Ahl al-Bayt* serves as the external social validation. The Imam’s comprehensive knowledge (*al-Ilm al-Shamil*) ensures he can answer any question, reflecting the Shia belief in the Imam's infallible authority to interpret the faith. This narrative underscores the continuity of spiritual leadership through both innate divine qualities and recognized scholarly excellence within the Prophet's lineage.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-13 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Abil Jarud, “I asked Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB), ‘May I be your ransom! If the most knowledgeable one from your household perishes, how can one know the Trustee who comes after him?’
The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘Through guidance, serenity, the testimony of the members of the Household of Muhammad (MGB) to his nobility, and his ability to respond to any questions asked.’”
